title: Transitivity on generic geometric specialization arrows over a normal base
statement: Let $N$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] that is normal, meaning that every local ring is a domain integrally closed in its fraction field, and let $\eta$ be its generic point [def-sc-generic-point]. Put $K=\kappa(\eta)$ [def-weil-residue-field], choose an algebraic closure $\overline K$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $\bar\eta:\operatorname{Spec}\overline K\to N$ be the resulting geometric generic point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let $\bar n$ be any geometric point of $N$. Regard $\bar\eta$ and $\bar n$ as points of $N_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with $2$-morphisms defined by natural transformations of direct images [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Then $\operatorname{Hom}_{N_{\mathrm{Et}}}(\bar\eta,\bar n)$ is nonempty, and for any two arrows $u,v:\bar\eta\Rightarrow\bar n$ there is an automorphism $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}_{N_{\mathrm{Et}}}(\bar\eta)$ with $u=v\circ\sigma$. Thus the right action on this Hom-set is precomposition $u\cdot\sigma=u\circ\sigma$, with the target geometric point fixed. Neither uniqueness of $\sigma$ nor a free action is asserted. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Orgogozo, proof of Lemma 8.3.2, printed p. 18 (PDF page index 17), the normal-base assertion that Aut(s′) acts transitively on Hom(s′,t′), following the integral-base reduction; auxiliary to lem-trf-local-term-locality (1)–(2).
